outputs.headline: False: 5G towers do not spread coronavirus
outputs.summary: The claim that 5G mobile towers spread the coronavirus is false; there is no scientific evidence to support this.
outputs.what_post_claims: The post claims that 5G mobile towers are responsible for spreading the coronavirus, leading to an increase in cases in areas where 5G was installed.
outputs.what_is_true: There is no scientific evidence linking 5G technology to the spread of the coronavirus. International health organizations and experts confirm that viruses cannot travel on radio waves or mobile networks.
evidence_against: The United Nations International Telecommunication Union (ITU) confirmed that 5G is not responsible for the spread of COVID-19, calling the conspiracy a 'hoax with no technical basis'.
AP News rated as false the claim that maps show a correlation between confirmed COVID-19 cases and where 5G wireless service has been installed.
AFP Fact Check rated as false the claim that coronavirus is a result of 5G.
outputs.sources_spoken: the United Nations International Telecommunication Union, AP News, and AFP Fact Check
outputs.audio_script: A post claims that 5G mobile towers are responsible for spreading the coronavirus, leading to an increase in cases where 5G was installed. This is false. There is no scientific evidence linking 5G technology to the spread of the coronavirus. International health organizations and experts confirm that viruses cannot travel on radio waves or mobile networks. We are very sure of this. This information comes from the United Nations International Telecommunication Union, AP News, and AFP Fact Check.
card_lines: Viruses cannot travel on radio waves
